In my opinion the best place to start with soulslikes. The combat feels very smooth (especially compared to the older Fromsoft games), the game features a lot of great and memorable enemies and bosses with some signature cryptic lore and amazing level design. I can't think of any particularly bad "quit moments", if anything the challenge and difficulty may put someone off, though you know very well what you're getting into. This game is an amazing adventure that's challenging, yet incredibly satisfying and I highly recommend it.

There are 3 types of enemies in Dark Souls 3.
Huge enemies - you hit the legs ( or hands in the case of one in particular in this instance ), and watch out for their slow but area wide and very powerful attacks.
Small enemies - you hit them on the back and they come in many different flavors, from slow and stupid to very quick and hard hitting. But all of thim, circle, defend/parry and attack them from behind.
And then there are dogs. Fuck dogs.

Dark Souls 3 is another one of my all time favourite soul games and probably my personal favourite in the trilogy. Playing through this game again was such a pleasure (most of the time) and nothing short of a truly sensational gaming experience. Some of the scenery and environments in this game really are a masterpiece and some of the most memorable moments in souls gaming history in terms of level and boss design, (Especially after leaving the catacombs and entering the irithyll of the boreal valley for the first time. Stunning! The eerie and Ominous feel to the game is chilling! Also nothing hits better than seeing the 'You Defeated' message on the screen after killing a boss with your awarded Soul Points followed by a nice shiny achievement. Beyond rewarding, a must play for all soul game lovers.

This is the second From Software game I was able to finish!
I dabbled with DS1 and Elden Ring, but then I got captivated by Sekiro. After 100 hours of Sekiro I thought I was ready to finish a Dark Souls game and so I did.

Compared to DS1 I got the impression getting around is a bit easier. The quests are still pretty obscure and it's very easy to miss important characters, but somehow this contribute to the sense of mistery of this franchise.

Overall this is really a pleasant game, I found most of the levels well designed and captivating.
It's very convenient to have a central hub (the firelink shrine).

If you played elden ring and are looking for a souls game perhaps this is a better start than DS1.

Aside from that though, it has some of the best bosses I've ever fought, both gameplay and design wise. With the main ones being Champion Gundyr, Dancer of The Boreal Valley, Dragonslayer Armor, Demon Prince, and Slave Knight Gael.

From the very beginning, Dark Souls III completely hooked me. Just minutes into the game, I was drawn in by its dark atmosphere, challenging enemies, and hauntingly beautiful music. It was my first Souls game, and it immediately won me over.
My favorite boss was definitely Pontiff Sulyvahn. That fight was a real challenge — I spent so many attempts trying to beat him. Every try taught me something new. I never gave up, and that sense of struggle and progress is exactly what makes this game so immersive.
Dark Souls III is more than just a game. It's a journey, an emotion, a test of will. If you haven't played it yet — I strongly recommend it. Be ready to die a lot... but every time, you'll rise stronger.

There is nothing like destroying a challenger who, extremely difficult at first, is bested once the complicated move set or boss rng is inherently mastered. Being incredibly perturbed is what this game is intended to accomplish on its players, but that feeling is slightly relived when the mere thoughts of beating the boss to make even more progression is prevalent in the superior gameplay loop from most metroidvania type games. The Dark Souls series not only aims to challenge its players, but it encourages them to strive for the hardest opponents. Take the tutorial boss, Iudex Gundyr for instance. The boss is extremely intimidating on first glance until us, the players, manages to see through the moveset, therefore improving at the mechanics and being able to take on even greater challenges. I recommend this game not just because of the challenge, but also because of the aesthetic, the playerbase, the fighting mechanics, the builds, and the overall lucrativity of progression that trully increases the satisfaction of the Dark Souls series.
